Judgment

This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from respondents on account of death of P. Suresh, husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 and 3, in Road Traffic Accident.

2. In brief, petition averments are; that on 15-08- 2019 at about 7.45 a.m., P. Suresh was riding his motor scooter, bearing No.KA-04-EW-5488 on Hesarghatta main road towards Bengaluru carefully and cautiously, when he reached near BESCOM Office, Sapthagiri College Junction, at that time the driver of lorry, bearing No.KA- 04-AA-3277 driven the same in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed, neglecting all traffic rules and regulations came from behind and dashed against P.
Suresh.
Due to the impact, he fell down, the lorry's left tyre ran over his head and he sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Earlier to the accident, the 3 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019 deceased was working as astrologer and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, on account of his untimely death petitioners lost the dependency, love and affection.
Hence, this petition for compensation.

, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C)
and 158(6) of M.V. Act, driver of lorry was not having valid and effective driving licence to drove the same, insured vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

3(a). Respondent No.2 contended that at the time of alleged accident deceased P. Suresh was riding his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner without following the traffic rules and he was riding behind the 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019 lorry, when he tried to overtake the same from the left side, due to imbalance he dashed against the left side back wheel of the said lorry, the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased himself.

Further, it contended that lorry, bearing Smt. B.S. Lakshmidevi vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171470827/

10. Spot mahazar and sketch, depict the incident.
Final report shows the negligence on the part of driver of the offended canter vehicle.
The IMV Report reveals that there was no mechanical defects in the vehicles.
The postmortem report shows the cause of death was due to head injury sustained.
According to the IMV report there was no mechanical defects in the vehicles in the sense the incident was due to the negligence only.
No independent eyewitness is examined herein.
Nothing is elicited from PW's in their cross-examination by respondents and also nothing is established by respondents regarding the negligence.

Here being no acceptable contrary evidence by respondents,
here is no impediment to believe the police documents regarding the negligence.
The police documents give right impression that due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the canter vehicle the incident occurred.

Regarding objections by respondent No.1 as to non compliance of provision under Section 134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act is concerned as the petition reached its finality and respondent No.2 is contesting the matter the giving of permission under Section 170 of MV Act, and discussion on the same now does not arise.
12.

Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that the P.
Suresh met with motor vehicle accident on 15.08.2019 at about 7.45 p.m., and sustained grievous injury and succumbed to the injury due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of canter vehicle, bearing No.KA-04- AA-3277. Hence, this issue is answered affirmatively.

sentences.text: In determination of this issue avocation, income, age of the deceased, dependency and future prospects and other conventional heads for compensation are need to be ascertained.
Avocation :
It is averred that the deceased was working as astrologer and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In substantiation of the same the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Hence, no other option but to consider notional income of the deceased in the present case.
As per Ex.P16-aadhar card, date of birth of the deceased was 12-05-1965 and so that age of the deceased was 54 years at the time of incident.
Hence, it is considered.
Income:
As discussed on the head of avocation, the deceased's avocation taken to be considered notionally.
In this regard as per the resolution of hon'ble the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dated 17-02- 2022 notional income for the year 2019 came to be fixed at 14,000/.
In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.14,000/- is taken to be considered as notional income of the deceased per month.
Dependency:
As per the petition averments petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are children of the deceased.
The dependency is not in dispute.
Ex.P12 to Ex.P15 - aadhar cards and ration card prove the identification of the petitioners.

Whereas, for deduction of personal expenses is concerned only 1/3rd is considered to be deducted in the monthly notional income, for the personal and living expenses of the deceased.
10 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019 Future prospects:
The future prospects is concerned, the age of the deceased at the time of the death was 54 years, so as per the principle laid down in Hem Raj vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others case, reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (SC), 10% needs to be added to the monthly notional income of the deceased.

sentences.text: So, 10% is added to the monthly income of the deceased.
Thus, 10% of addition will come to Rs.1,400/-.
In total, the monthly notional income will be Rs.15,400/-.

sentences.text: Conventional Heads:

As conventional heads, the deceased being husband of petitioner No.1 spousal consortium and father of petitioner No.2 and 3 parental consortium are to be considered as the petitioners suffered the loss of love and affection.

Hence, in view of the observations made, in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others, in civil Appeal No.2705/2020, by hon'ble the Apex Court, Rs.40,000/- each is considered to be awarded as compensation for consortium respectively.

sentences.text: The loss of estate is concerned, as the deceased was with the family, if the incident could not have been occurred, he could have been contributed more or less from his savings to the estate of the family; the incident caused such loss to the estate of the petitioners.

Hence, Rs.15,000/- is need to be awarded on this head as the 11 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019 principle laid down by hon'ble the Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, and others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

sentences.text: Likewise, for the funeral expenses is concerned awarding of Rs.15,000/- is also just under the conventional head as observed by hon'ble the Apex Court.
Hence, it is considered to be awarded.

14. Accordingly, compensation is calculated as under;
Monthly notional income of Rs.14,000/-.
Future prospects in 10% on the monthly notional income is Rs.1,400/-.
Monthly notional income + future prospects = 15,400/-.
For personal and living expenses, after the deduction of 1/3rd, the total monthly notional income is Rs.10,267/-.
Net monthly notional income is Rs.10,267/- is calculated to net annul income as Rs.10,267/- x 12 which is = 1,23,204/-.
Multiplier is 11.
Net annual notional income is multiplied by multiplier 11, which is as Rs.1,23,204/- x 11, will come to Rs.13,55,244/-.

15. So, compensation for loss of dependency is found at Rs.13,55,244/- plus compensation on 12 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019 conventional heads, such as spousal and parental consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is considered to be directed till its realization.
So, the petitioners are entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.

Liability:
18. Insurance policy and its validity are admitted but a breech of insurance policy condition i.e.,
driver of respondent No.2/RW4 was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of incident as the offended vehicle is not of class of LMV.
As per evidence 13 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019 of RW-2 coupled with Ex.R-9 the driver had LMV driving license as on the date of incident.
Ex.R-8 coupled with admission of RW-2 that the offended vehicle is of unladen weight of 4300 Kgs.
Such being the case, herein observations in Civil Appeal No.5826/2011, in the case of Mukund Devagan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., made by hon'ble Apex Court are applicable.

entities.text: Mukund Devagan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that "definition of light motor vehicle makes it clear that for a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which or a motor car or tractor or road-roller the unladen weight of any of which, does not exceed 7500 kgs.
Gross vehicle weight has been defined in Section 2(15).
The motor car or tractor or road roller, the unladen weight of any of which does not exceed 7500 kgs. as defined in Section 2(48) of the Act, or also the light motor vehicle.
No change has been made by amendment act of 54/94 in the provisions contained in Sections 2(21) and 10(2)(d) relating to the light motor vehicle.

Definition of light motor vehicle has to be given full effect to and it has to be read with Section 10(2)(d) which makes it abundantly clear that light motor vehicle is also a transport vehicle, the gross vehicle weight or unladen weight of which does not exceed 7500 kgs. as specified in the provision.

Thus, a driver is issued a licence as per the class of vehicle i.e., light motor vehicle, transport vehicle or omnibus or another vehicle of other categories as per gross vehicle weight or unladen weight as specified in Section 2(21) of 14 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019 the Act.
The provision of Section 3 of the Act requires that a person in order to drive a transport vehicle must have authorization.

Once a licence is issued to drive light motor vehicle, it would also mean specific authorization to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight or motor car, road roller or tractor, the unladen weight of which, as the case may be, does not exceed 7500 kg...."
According to the above observation, in the present case the offending vehicle being vehicle of unladen weight of 4300 kgs, which does not exceed 7500 kgs.
in its gross weight, the insurer will not be allowed to avoid its liability merely for technical breach of conditions concerning driving licence.

As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the driver of the car, on vicarious liability respondent No.2 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.1 being the insurer of respondent No.2 liable to pay the compensation in the light of the above observation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially the first respondent is liable to pay the determined compensation.

The petitioner is only entitled to such 15 (SCCH-16)
MVC 5222/2019 compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

21.
In view of the findings, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.
Hence, the following order is passed:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,05,300/- (Rupees fifteen lakhs, five thousand and three hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.

However,
the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 -Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Compensation amount is  apportioned as follows:-
 Petitioner No.1 - Wife 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - Son 25%
 Petitioner No.3 - Son 25%
 16 (SCCH-16) MVC 5222/2019

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner No.1 to 3, 25% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as FD in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 75% amount with proportionate interest shall be released to them through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
